headline: After a cooler, cloudier weekend with light rain Sunday night into Monday, a strong and unusual storm on Tuesday into early Wednesday is expected to dump 1 to 3 inches on the coast and valleys and 3 to 5 inches in the foothills, heaviest in Los Angeles County, with a higher-than-normal risk of severe thunderstorms — people near recent burn areas should prepare now.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Saturday's sunny skies give way to a broad sheet of high clouds ahead of the coming storm, and a switch to ocean breezes in the afternoon cools most areas, including Glendale and the LA valleys, by 3 to 6 degrees. Even so, highs end up 4 to 8 degrees above normal. Saturday night stays dry.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Sunday is mostly cloudy and another 3 to 6 degrees cooler, with a 20 to 30 percent chance of light rain on the Central Coast in the afternoon. Light rain likely develops on the Central Coast Sunday evening and spreads into Los Angeles County by dawn Monday, with less than a tenth of an inch overnight except up to a quarter inch north of Morro Bay. Monday is cloudy with on-and-off showers, especially on the coastal slopes and foothills, with totals no more than a quarter inch and more likely under a tenth; highs drop to the mid 60s to low 70s.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A large, strong storm hits early Tuesday through early Wednesday, taking an unusual track that brings its center near or over the area into San Diego County; this favors thunderstorms with a greater-than-normal threat of severe weather, and it will hit Los Angeles and Ventura counties much harder than San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties. Rain totals will likely be 1 to 3 inches for the coast and valleys and 3 to 5 inches for the coastal slopes and foothills, highest in Los Angeles County, with a 20 percent chance totals run an inch or two higher; rain rates can reach an inch per hour in the foothills and near 1.5 inches per hour in thunderstorms, so residents near recent burn scars should prepare to protect property and plan for possible evacuations. Rain tapers off Tuesday night into early Wednesday, leaving a mostly dry, clearing Wednesday with highs in the mid 60s to low 70s, then a sunny Thursday near normal with light offshore winds. Another storm arrives Friday, with most forecasts showing around a quarter inch, though a few now show heavier rain.

coast: A large, long-period west swell keeps easing, but high surf continues through Saturday afternoon on the Central Coast and the Ventura and Los Angeles County coasts, with strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, some risk of sneaker waves, heavy shore break and beach erosion making swimming dangerous; High Surf Advisories run until 4 PM or 9 PM Saturday depending on the stretch of coast, and a Beach Hazards Statement covers other beaches through Saturday afternoon. An exceptionally high tide of up to 7.2 feet Saturday morning brings a threat of minor to moderate flooding in low-lying coastal spots, with a Coastal Flood Advisory for the Ventura County beaches until 4 PM Saturday. On the water, a Small Craft Advisory runs until 3 AM Saturday for parts of the waters; conditions stay mostly calmer through Monday evening, then winds and seas build Monday night and reach gale force Tuesday across all coastal waters, with hazardous seas, squalls with thunderstorms, possible waterspouts and poor visibility in heavy rain. Advisory-level winds and seas linger into Wednesday, with a 50 percent chance of gales Wednesday night on the outer waters.
watch_for: Flooding and debris flows near recent burn scars during Tuesday's heavy rain
Severe thunderstorms with very heavy downpours Tuesday, especially in LA County
Friday's follow-up storm, which a few forecasts now show as wetter
confidence: Forecasters have quite high confidence in Tuesday's major storm because the computer models have been very consistent (perhaps trending slightly south), though exact totals depend on the storm's speed and track; Friday's storm is less certain.
